<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing a system design/architecture diagram for the TrackWeight macOS application. We’ll break the project into its core components, show how they interact, and outline best practices for diagramming.

1. Identify Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a native macOS desktop application (built in Swift 6+/Xcode 16) that uses Force Touch trackpad sensors for weight measurement.  
   - It follows an MVVM-style pattern with a SwiftUI frontend, Combine for reactive data flow, and a low-level touch library (OpenMultitouchSupport) for sensor access.

2. Analyze File Structure  
   Top-level modules:  
   - Sources/OpenMultitouchSupport (OMS library)  
     • OMSManager.swift – Touch event capture and publisher  
     • OMSTouchData.swift – Touch data model (pressure, position, etc.)  
   - TrackWeight (app code)  
     • TrackWeightApp.swift – App entry point  
     • *.swift views (ContentView, ScaleView, WeighingView, DebugView, etc.)  
     • *ViewModel.swift (ContentViewModel, ScaleViewModel, WeighingViewModel)  
     • WeighingState.swift – Domain state model  
     • Assets & entitlements

3. Main Components to Represent  
   a. User Interface Layer (SwiftUI Views)  
      - ContentView, HomeView, ScaleView, TrackWeightView, DebugView  
   b. Presentation / ViewModel Layer (Combine publishers/subscribers)  
      - ContentViewModel, ScaleViewModel, WeighingViewModel  
   c. Core Logic / Domain Model  
      - WeighingState, calibration logic, pressure-to-weight conversion  
   d. Sensor Integration Library  
      - OpenMultitouchSupport (OMSManager + OMSTouchData)  
   e. Operating System & Hardware  
      - macOS event system, Force Touch trackpad hardware  
   f. Build & Deployment  
      - Xcode project, Package.swift, Homebrew cask workflow

4. Relationships & Data Flow  
   1. User taps/places finger on trackpad → SwiftUI View reacts to ViewModel state  
   2. ViewModel subscribes to OMSManager pressure data publisher  
   3. OMSManager captures raw touch events via private macOS APIs → emits OMSTouchData streams  
   4. ViewModel receives pressure readings → applies calibration logic in WeighingState → computes weight  
   5. ViewModel publishes weight updates → SwiftUI View displays updated measurement  
   6. DebugView optionally subscribes to raw OMSTouchData for logging  
   7. Build pipeline: GitHub Actions updates Homebrew formula for distribution  

5. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) separation  
   - Reactive data flow via Combine (Publishers & Subscribers)  
   - Single responsibility per ViewModel (each view has its own)  
   - Modular dependency on an external library (OpenMultitouchSupport)  
   - Sandbox disabled for low-level hardware access  

6. Drawing the Diagram  
   a. Use distinct shapes/colors:  
      - Blue rectangles for UI Views  
      - Green cylinders or hexagons for ViewModels (presentation layer)  
      - Yellow boxes for domain logic/state  
      - Orange boxes for external library/module  
      - Gray cloud/box for macOS + Trackpad hardware  
      - Dashed box around build/deploy pipeline  

   b. Arrows & Labels:  
      - Unidirectional arrows from hardware → OMSManager → ViewModel → View → User  
      - Label data flows (e.g., “pressure readings”, “weight measurement”, “UI events”)  
      - Show event streams with lightning-bolt icons or arrowheads  

   c. Grouping & Swimlanes:  
      - Leftmost lane: Hardware & OS  
      - Next lane: OMS Library  
      - Center lane: Domain/Logic (WeighingState)  
      - Next lane: Presentation (ViewModels)  
      - Right lane: UI Layer  

7. Tailoring Diagram to TrackWeight  
   - Emphasize the hardware integration path (Force Touch → OpenMultitouchSupport → App)  
   - Show Combine pipelines explicitly (Publisher → map/transform → Subscriber)  
   - Highlight calibration step in domain logic  
   - Depict the sandbox-disabled entitlement as a prerequisite for sensor access  

8. Diagram Annotation Checklist  
   - Clear component labels (e.g., “OMSManager”, “WeighingViewModel”)  
   - Arrowheads indicating direction of control/data flow  
   - Color-coding legend for component types (UI, ViewModel, Domain, External, Hardware)  
   - Notes on protocols or frameworks (SwiftUI, Combine, Swift Package)  
   - Boundary boxes to show module/package separation  
   - Optionally include build workflow snippet (GitHub Actions → Homebrew formula)

By breaking the system into these layers and drawing explicit data flows and dependencies, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate architecture diagram that highlights both the MVVM structure and the unique hardware integration path of TrackWeight.  
Ensure each component is individually labeled, use arrows for all interactions, and apply consistent color or shape conventions to make the diagram visually clear and easy to understand.  
</explanation>
